claims.text: The target materials are high-melting refractory materials.
An ab initio free-energy approach based on DFT can accurately calculate the melting properties of high-melting refractory materials.
Machine-learning-based interpolation can reduce the computational cost of the ab initio free-energy approach.
The materials are initially in the solid state.
The proposed intervention combines DFT-based ab initio free-energy calculations with machine-learning interpolation.
The method is intended for high-temperature and high-pressure conditions.
Electronic structure and atomic arrangements act as the structural mediator.
The mechanism involves thermodynamic integration using ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations.
Machine-learning interpolation within the thermodynamic-integration workflow reduces computational cost.
The method can accurately calculate melting temperature, entropy of fusion, enthalpy of fusion, and volume change at the melting point.
Experimental measurements provide the baseline for evaluating the calculations.
The method is limited by available computational resources and by the accuracy of the machine-learning interpolation.
The interpolation model may not transfer reliably across different materials and conditions.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing calculated melting properties with experimental measurements for multiple refractory materials.
A significant deviation between calculated and experimental melting properties would falsify the hypothesis.
